Every creative records its campaign, who submitted it, its risk rating, its content tags, and its status.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages advertising campaigns and their budget approval for an ad agency.
The people involved are advertisers, account managers, brand safety reviewers, and campaign directors, and one person may hold both the account manager and campaign director roles at the same time.
The resources are campaigns and creatives.
Every campaign records its advertiser, the account manager who prepared it, its budget, its contingency amount, its budget tier, its risk labels, its scheduled start, and its status.
Every creative records its campaign, the person who submitted it, its risk rating, its content tags, and its status.
Each requester carries a reviewer level, and each request carries the current time, whether multi-factor authentication was used, whether the device is trusted, and whether the launch is an emergency.
An account manager or a campaign director may approve a campaign's budget.
The account manager who prepared a campaign may not approve its own budget.
A campaign director who did not prepare the campaign may approve its budget even though the account manager who prepared it may not.
Neither an account manager nor a campaign director may approve a budget when the campaign's budget plus its contingency exceeds $500,000.
When the campaign's budget plus its contingency is $500,000 or less, an account manager or campaign director who did not prepare the campaign may approve it without that restriction.
Neither an account manager nor a campaign director may approve a budget unless multi-factor authentication was used for the request.
When multi-factor authentication was used, an account manager or campaign director who did not prepare the campaign may approve a qualifying budget.
An account manager must not approve the budget of a campaign they prepared, and a campaign director must not approve the budget of a campaign they prepared either.
A request by a campaign director who did not prepare a campaign, made with multi-factor authentication, to approve a budget of $500,000 or less must be able to succeed.

A payout officer or claims manager must not use the payment-cutoff exception outside the payment-cutoff window.

A request by a payout officer to issue a payout that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

When the request does not come from the on-property network, the requested-state requirement does not bind the authorization.

Neither a shift manager nor a front office manager may authorize a comp outside the requested state when the item threshold is crossed and the request comes from the on-property network.

A request by a shift manager to authorize a comp that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Cedar Schema
```cedar
entity Person {
    roles: Set<String>,
    signingAuthority: Long,
    conflictedCounterparties: Set<String>,
};

entity Contract {
    drafter: Person,
    reviewer: Person,
    counterparty: String,
    contractValue: Long,
    requiredAuthority: Long,
    effectiveDate: datetime,
    status: String,
    reviewWindowStart: datetime,
    reviewWindowEnd: datetime,
};

entity Signature;

entity Role enum ["Drafter", "Reviewer", "Signatory"];

action reviewContract appliesTo {
    principal: [Person],
    resource: [Contract],
    context: {
        currentDate: datetime,
        onCorporateNetwork: Bool,
        mfaUsed: Bool,
        escalationApproved: Bool,
        organizationMoneyThreshold: Long,
    },
};
```

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages the review stage of contract lifecycle management.

The people involved are drafters, reviewers, signatories, and contract admins. One person may hold both the drafter and reviewer roles, and one person may hold both the reviewer and signatory roles.

The resources are contracts and signatures. Every contract records its drafter, reviewer, counterparty, contract value, required authority, effective date, and status.

Each requester carries their signing authority and conflicted counterparties.

Each request carries the current date, whether it is made on the corporate network, whether multi-factor authentication was used, and whether escalation was approved.

A reviewer who drafted a contract may not review it when the contract value crosses the organization's money threshold and the request falls within the permitted review window.

For contracts that do not cross the organization's money threshold, the drafter may review their own contract.

Outside the permitted review window, the drafter-review separation rule does not bind the review request.

A reviewer who did not draft a contract may review it when the request falls within the permitted review window and the contract otherwise trips no prohibition above.

A request by a reviewer to review a contract that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Cedar Schema
```cedar
entity User {
    isCalibrationTechnician: Bool,
    isSeniorTechnician: Bool,
    isMetrologyManager: Bool,
    isQualityInspector: Bool,
    isMaintenanceSupervisor: Bool,
};

entity Asset {
    technician: User,
    equipmentClass: String,
    status: String,
    calibrationDueDate: datetime,
    outOfService: Bool,
    measurementPointCount: Long,
    assetTag: String,
    hazardClass: String,
    hasHazardousMaterialTag: Bool,
};

entity CalibrationRecord {
    asset: Asset,
    technician: User,
    result: String,
    calibrationTime: datetime,
};

action approveReturnToService appliesTo {
    principal: [User],
    resource: [Asset],
    context: {
        currentTime: datetime,
        onPlantNetwork: Bool,
        cleanRoomCertified: Bool,
        emergencyDeclared: Bool,
    },
};
```

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages calibrated equipment and return-to-service approval.

The people involved are calibration technicians, senior technicians, metrology managers, quality inspectors, and maintenance supervisors. One person may hold both the calibration technician and senior technician role at the same time.

The resources are assets and calibration records. Every asset records its technician, equipment class, status, calibration due date, out-of-service marker, measurement point count, asset tag, and hazard class.

Each calibration record records its asset, technician, result, and calibration time.

Each request carries the current time, whether it is on the plant network, whether the requester is clean-room certified, and whether an emergency has been declared.

A quality inspector or metrology manager may approve return to service only after a hazardous-material asset reaches calibrated status.

For an asset without a hazardous-material tag, the calibrated-status requirement does not apply under this rule.

A quality inspector must not approve return to service for a hazardous-material asset that has not reached calibrated status.

A metrology manager must not approve return to service for a hazardous-material asset that has not reached calibrated status.

A request by a quality inspector to approve a return to service that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

entity User {
    isPlanner: Bool,
    isShiftSupervisor: Bool,
    isOperator: Bool,
    isControlRoomOperator: Bool,
    isAuditor: Bool,
};

    planner: User,
    executor: User,
    feeder: String,
    voltageLevel: String,
    circuitCount: Long,
    status: String,
    scheduledStart: datetime,
    scheduledEnd: datetime,
};

entity LockoutTag;

action authorizeSwitching appliesTo {
    principal: [User],
    resource: [SwitchingOrder],
    context: {
        currentTime: datetime,
        fromSCADAControlNetwork: Bool,
        lockoutTagoutVerified: Bool,
        outageEmergencyDeclared: Bool,
    },
};

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages switching orders for grid operations and field execution.

The people involved are planners, shift supervisors, operators, control room operators, and auditors. One person may hold both the planner and shift supervisor roles, or both the operator and control room operator roles, at the same time.

The resources are switching orders and lockout tags. Every switching order records its planner, executor, feeder, voltage level, circuit count, status, scheduled start, and scheduled end.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the SCADA control network, whether lockout tagout has been verified, and whether an outage emergency has been declared.

A planner or shift supervisor may authorize switching only after lockout tagout has been verified in the control room.

When lockout tagout has not been verified in the control room, neither a planner nor a shift supervisor may authorize switching.

A planner or shift supervisor may authorize switching only when the request comes from the SCADA control network.

When the request does not come from the SCADA control network, neither a planner nor a shift supervisor may authorize switching.

Neither a planner nor a shift supervisor may authorize a switching order if they are the field operator designated to execute that order.

A request by a planner to authorize a switching order that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages authorization of prescription refills at an outpatient pharmacy that dispenses controlled substances.

The people involved are pharmacy technicians, staff pharmacists, pharmacists in charge, and prescribers, and one person may hold both the staff pharmacist and the pharmacist in charge role at the same time.

The resources are prescriptions and dispense records.

Every prescription records its prescriber, its patient, who entered it, who verified it, the prescriber's DEA registration number, its controlled-substance schedule level, its refills remaining, and its status.

Every dispense record records its prescription, who dispensed it, the quantity dispensed, and the copay amount.

A pharmacist in charge may authorize a refill for a prescription only if they are the same pharmacist who originally verified that prescription.

A pharmacist in charge who did not verify a prescription must not authorize its refill, even if they are otherwise qualified to do so.

A pharmacist in charge may authorize a refill only when the prescription still has at least one refill remaining.

When a prescription has zero refills remaining, no pharmacist in charge, including the one who verified it, may authorize a further refill.

A pharmacist in charge may authorize a refill only when the prescriber's DEA registration number matches a valid, recognized format.

When the prescriber's DEA registration number does not match a valid format, the refill must not be authorized, even by the pharmacist in charge who verified the prescription.

A request by a pharmacist in charge to authorize a refill for a prescription that they verified, that still has refills remaining, and whose prescriber has a valid DEA registration number, must be able to succeed.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages controlled-substance prescriptions and refills in an outpatient pharmacy.

The people involved are pharmacy technicians, staff pharmacists, pharmacists in charge, and prescribers. One person may hold both the staff pharmacist and pharmacist in charge roles at the same time.

The resources are prescriptions and dispense records. Every prescription records its prescriber, patient, entered by, verified by, prescriber DEA, schedule level, refills remaining, and status.

Each requester carries dispense authority and a state license.

Each request carries whether the prescription-drug-monitoring database was checked, whether MFA was used, whether the requester is on the pharmacy network, the current time, and whether an emergency override is being used.

The pharmacist in charge who authorizes a refill must be the same pharmacist who verified the prescription.

A pharmacist in charge who did not verify the prescription must not authorize its refill.

Outside pharmacy operating hours, a pharmacist in charge may authorize a refill only when the prescription-drug-monitoring database was checked before the refill.

During pharmacy operating hours, the operating-hours exception relaxes the prescription-drug-monitoring database check requirement for authorizing a refill.

A request by a pharmacist in charge to authorize a refill that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

When the prescriber's DEA registration number does not match the allowed pattern, a pharmacist in charge must not authorize the refill.

During pharmacy operating hours, the time-of-request check does not block the refill authorization.

Outside pharmacy operating hours, a pharmacist in charge must not authorize the refill.

A request by a pharmacist in charge to authorize a refill that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages authorization of bank wire transfers.

The people involved are originators, verifiers, treasury officers, and compliance reviewers. One person may hold both the originator and the verifier role at the same time.

The resources are wire transfers and accounts. Every wire transfer records who initiated it, who verified it, who screened it, its account, amount, fee, amount tier, beneficiary, currency code, high-risk marking, and status.

Every account records its holder and its allowed beneficiaries.

Each requester carries an approval tier.

Each request carries the current time, the daily cutoff, whether it is on the secure network, whether multi-factor authentication was used, and whether an emergency has been declared.

A verifier or treasury officer may approve a wire only when their approval tier is at least as high as the wire's amount tier.

A verifier or treasury officer may approve a wire only when the beneficiary is on the account's screened allowlist.

A verifier or treasury officer may approve a wire only when the amount plus the fee crosses the required review threshold.

A verifier and a treasury officer must not approve a wire when their approval tier is below the wire's amount tier.

A request by a verifier to approve a wire that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

A request by a verifier to approve a wire that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.
